note: Andhra explorations (Stone Age tools around Dharanikota) and Kesarapalli excavation; no identification.

author: Sita Ram Roy, K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (Vaisali); Raghbir Singh, Mid-eastern Circle, ASI (Rajgir)
name_in_asr: Vaisali (Baniya, Virpur, stupa near the Chaturmukha-Mahadeva temple); New Fort at Rajgir
asr_identification: Vaisali = Basarh area (Muzaffarpur); New Fort, Rajgir (Patna), outside the hill-girt valley = the new city ascribed to Ajatasatru
evidence: Vaisali 1961-62: Baniya a single NBP period; NBP ware below the stupa near the Chaturmukha-Mahadeva temple confirmed; Virpur three periods. Rajgir: 66-m cutting across the S defences of the New Fort: pre-defence habitation with NBP, iron and a hoard of 14 punch-marked coins, ended by a conflagration; then a mud rampart (Period IIA) with brick retaining wall and moat
quote: undertook excavation at the New Fort at Rajgir, situated outside the hill-girt valley, supposed to have been founded by Ajatasatru, the Magadhan contemporary of Buddha … The excavation near the Chaturmukha-Mahadeva temple confirmed the last year's findings regarding the occurrence of the N.B.P. Ware below the stupa
note: New Fort = Mizutani's New Rajagrha (09.02.18: ruins on the plain N of the old city's N gate); Xuanzang ascribes the new city to Bimbisara and gives Ajatasatru as a variant; the dig dates the habitation, not the attribution. Vaisali stupa: early stupa in the Basarh area (07.03), not tied to any of Xuanzang's stupas (cf. 106 in batch 1).
Shamlaji excavation; Vadnagar Period III pottery compared (Anandapura, 11.09, not discussed).

author: G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University
asr_identification: palace-complex in the SW corner of Kosam (Allahabad), on the Yamuna
evidence: 1961-62: stone palace founded early in Phase I B, c. 8th c. BC (four of five layers against its wall pre-NBP); Phase II (NBP) SE tower on the Yamuna, W boundary wall, dressed-stone drain; Phase III three blocks with an audience hall, true arches and underground chambers, last structural phase c. 1st-2nd c. AD
quote: The University of Allahabad resumed (1960-61, p. 33) excavation of the palace area at Kausambi under Professor G.R. Sharma … The first phase of the palace, therefore, could be dated to circa eighth century B.C.
note: Continues 109-110 (batch 1). Xuanzang puts Udayana's sandalwood image in a vihara within the old palace of Kausambi (05.05); this palace is a candidate, but the report names neither Udayana nor Xuanzang, and its last phase (1st-2nd c. AD) is long before him. City = Kosam as Mizutani, asr and ar.
Explorations around Allahabad and Varanasi (NBP sites, megaliths), Ayodhya mounds re-explored; Rajgir masonry compared; no identification.

author: D. Mitra, Eastern Circle, ASI (Nepal tarai expedition, with the Department of Archaeology, Nepal)
asr_identification: Lumbini (Rummindei, Bhairwa district); Tilaura-kot, early city-site N of Taulihawa (Nepal tarai)
evidence: expedition Feb.-May 1962 based at Lumbini; Lumbini yields grey ware and antiquities from the 3rd c. BC to at least the 9th c. AD; sites in Bhairwa and Taulihawa districts explored; Tilaura-kot and Kudan excavated
quote: With Lumbini as its temporary headquarters, the party covered much new ground and discovered and examined a large number of sites in Bhairwa and Taulihawa Districts and later on shifted itself to Ramghat for the excavation of the early city-site of Tilaura-kot … from Lumbini, the starting-point of the exploration, which itself was found to contain sherds of grey ware and antiquities ranging from the third century B.C. to at least the ninth century A.D.
note: Summary; detail in 130-132. Occupation at Lumbini through the 7th c. fits Mizutani's Rummindei (06.02.11, 06.02.12) and Xuanzang's visit; no identification argued.

author: D. Mitra, Eastern Circle, ASI (Nepal tarai expedition)
asr_identification: the 14 sites of P. C. Mukherji's 1899 tour revisited (Taulihawa district, Nepal); Gotihawa with the lower part of an Asokan pillar in situ
evidence: Mukherji's descriptions found generally correct but his structures badly damaged; Sisania mound rich in early pottery and Kushan coins; Kudan (2 km SW of Taulihawa, 3 km NE of Gotihawa) excavated: well with carved brick platform and two Brahmanical brick temples (linga, Mahishasuramardini), early medieval
quote: fourteen sites, viz. Araura-kot, Bijua, Bikuli, Chatradi, Dohni, Siwalwa, Gotihawa, Kudan, Nigali-sagar, Sagarwa, Sisahnia, Sisania, Taulihawa and Tilaura-kot, which had been visited by P.C. Mukherji in 1899, were revisited … some 3 km. to the north-east of Gotihawa, where there exists in situ the lower portion of an Asokan pillar
note: No identification. Gotihawa (often taken for Krakucchanda's pillar, 06.02.05; Mizutani gives no site) and Nigali-sagar (Mizutani's Kanakamuni pillar, 06.02.05a) are only named. Kudan (Mukherji's Lori-ki-kudan) yields only Brahmanical temples; not connected with any of Xuanzang's sites.

author: D. Mitra, Eastern Circle, ASI (Nepal tarai expedition)
asr_identification: fortified mound of Tilaura-kot, 3 km NNE of Taulihawa (Nepal)
evidence: trench across the N fortification near the NW corner, 3.80 m deposit: Period I pre-defence habitation (1.50 m) from the advent of NBP ware, ring-wells, brick structures, ending in a conflagration; Period II mud rampart with moat and a brick fortification wall c. 4 m wide; Mauryan-Sunga terracottas, punch-marked and cast coins
quote: a small-scale excavation was undertaken at the jungle-clad, wild-animal-infested fortified mound of Tilaura-kot, which is at a straight distance of 3 km. to the north-north-east of Taulihawa … was coeval with the advent at the site of the Northern Black Polished Ware
note: Detail of the dig summarised in 132; the stratigraphy dates the city wall but contains nothing of Xuanzang's period.

author: D. Mitra, Eastern Circle, ASI (Nepal tarai expedition)
asr_identification: Tilaura-kot (Taulihawa district, Nepal): identification with Kapilavastu neither established nor disproved
evidence: small trench yielded 5 gold objects, 65 coins (2 silver punch-marked), 27 terracotta figurines of the 3rd-1st c. BC, two terracotta sealings (one inscribed), over 340 beads, a Mathura-school head; Panchala coins and Kushan terracottas on the surface
quote: Tilaura-kot was identified in the past by some archaeologists with ancient Kapilavastu, but the excavation has not yielded anything to establish or disprove the identification.
note: Mizutani 06.02 = old city near Tilaurakot; the 1962 dig is explicitly neutral. The inscribed sealing is not read here. The rival claim from the Piprahwa-Ganwaria sealings (K. M. Srivastava) comes later.
Epigraphy (Satavahana pillar inscription at Nagarjunakonda; charters); no location.
Epigraphy (Tamil inscriptions); 'kesariya' an OCR match in 'Arikesariyan'.
Coins (Kausambi nigama coins) and minor discoveries; no location.
Explorations; Ganwari near Piprahwa (later Ganwaria) found to yield grey ware and NBP; no identification proposed.

Plate captions (Lumbini bronzes, Kudan, Tilaura-kot coins); see 131-132.
Contents and plate list.

author: M. Venkataramayya, South-eastern Circle, ASI
asr_identification: fortified township at Dharanikota on the right bank of the Krishna (Guntur)
evidence: cutting across the W side: seven structural phases, six of an embankment-cum-wharf on a navigation channel cut into a laterite ridge (wooden-post wharf, then brick wharf), the last the defence system
quote: conducted excavation at Dharanikota, situated on the right bank of the Krishna river. A cutting laid across the western side of the fortified township revealed seven structural Phases, of which the earlier six related to the embankment-cum-wharf abutting a navigation-channel, and the latest one to the defence-system.
note: The report names neither Dhanyakataka nor Xuanzang. A fortified river town at Dharanikota supports Mizutani's capital of 10.14 near Dharanikota (against Bezwada) and his Avarasaila at Dharanikota (10.14.02b); nothing of the 7th c. reported.

author: Raghbir Singh, Mid-eastern Circle, ASI
asr_identification: New Fort, Rajgir (Patna): habitation area and S defences
evidence: same three periods in the habitation area as in the 1961-62 cutting; NBP in the pre-rampart levels; C-14 of pre-rampart charcoal 245 ± 105 BC; hoard of bone styluses or arrow-heads in Sub-period III B; second cutting across the S defences near the SE corner to relate the brick fortifications to the rubble wall: Period I NBP with rubble walls and storage jars
quote: The resumed excavation (1961-62, p. 7) at Rajgir by the Mid-eastern Circle of the Survey, under Shri Raghbir Singh, brought to light the same sequence of three Periods in the habitation-area as revealed last year in the cutting across the defences … With a view to investigating the relationship of the brick fortifications with the enormous rubble fortification wall
note: Continues 125. New Rajagrha as Mizutani 09.02.18; the C-14 date puts the rampart after c. 245 BC, later than the traditional Ajatasatru/Bimbisara foundation; the report does not draw the conclusion.
Kaveripattinam excavation; Nagarjunakonda brick size compared.

author: G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University
asr_identification: palace-complex in the extreme SW corner of Kosam (Allahabad)
evidence: 1962-63: twofold sequence confirmed: undressed stone wall with central-Indian chalcolithic painted pottery, then dressed masonry in the NBP phase; mud rampart on the S side against attack and Yamuna floods
quote: resumed the excavations of the palace-area in the extreme south-west corner, primarily with a view to confirming the structural sequence observed last year … This wall evidently served a dual purpose, viz. to defend the city in case of attack and to save it from the floods of the Yamuna.
note: Continues 127; no reference to Udayana or Xuanzang. City = Kosam as Mizutani (05.05).
Explorations; Rangamatia (Midnapur) is not Rangamati.

author: S. R. Das, Department of Archaeology, University of Calcutta
asr_identification: Rajbadi-danga at Jadupur, over 1 km from Chiruti station (Murshidabad) = the Raktamrittika monastery in the suburbs of Karnasuvarna
evidence: 1962-63: five structural phases (c. 3rd-4th c. to 12th c.); Phase III (6th-7th c.) platform, two circular basements probably of a stupa, lime-plastered steps; Phase V carved-brick structures with pradakshina-patha; seals with the Buddhist formula; a Phase III sealing naming Rakta-mrittika-mahavihara; Gupta stucco heads
quote: With a view to identifying Karnasuvarna, the traditional capital-city of Sasanka with its stupas, monasteries and other monuments mentioned by Hiuen Tsang … One of them, from Phase III (pl. XC D), mentioned Rakta-mrittika-mahavihara, described by Hiuen Tsang to be situated in the suburbs of Karnasuvarna, the capital of Gauda in the seventh century.
note: Inscribed find naming the monastery: confirms Mizutani's 10.08.02 (Raktamrttika at Rangamati) and puts Karnasuvarna's capital beside it, as Mizutani's 10.08 (Rangamati). Against Beglar's Dulmi/Sapharan (asr); settles the doubt of Dikshit (ar, Eastern Circle 1920-21) for the monastery, though not for the capital itself.
Minor discoveries in Andhra (Amaravati limestone).
Museums (Kausambi Udayana-Vasavadatta plaque).
Museums.
Conservation (Vaisali, Nalanda).
Chemistry and gardens.
Publications.

author: M. Venkataramayya, assisted by K. Raghavachari, South-eastern Circle, ASI
asr_identification: rectangular fort at Dharanikota (Guntur) with navigation channel and reservoir
evidence: 1963-64: cuttings DKT-2 and DKT-3; the fort-wall phases of DKT-1 recorded on its E half (laterite reinforcement in Phase V); a reservoir bund (tank called Hamsala-Gundam) with glass objects, Rouletted and NBP wares; brick revetment of the navigation channel confirmed along the S wall of the rectangular fort
quote: The existence at this place of a water-reservoir called Hamsala-Gundam, which in course of time got filled up, lends support to this belief … Cutting DKT-3 (fig. 1) was laid across the southern wall of the rectangular fort-wall.
note: Continues 147; no reference to Dhanyakataka or Xuanzang. Bears on Mizutani's capital near Dharanikota (10.14) and Avarasaila (10.14.02b).

author: Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture, Panjab University
asr_identification: ancient site of Sugh, 5 km E of Jagadhri (Ambala)
evidence: 1963-64 small-scale dig: NBP with grey ware, one PGW sherd at the lowest levels; Sunga-Kushan terracottas, cast coins; 1.6 km W, a large rectangular burnt-brick structure (wall 1.5 m thick, bricks 50 x 26 x 10 cm), a fortress or a monastery enclosure
quote: undertook a small-scale excavation at the ancient site of Sugh, about 5 km. cast of Jagadhari … About 1.6 km. to the west of the site were noticed remains of a large rectangular burnt-brick structure of early historical period, which seemed to be either a fortress or an enclosure of some monastery.
note: Sugh as Cunningham (asr) and Mizutani 04.09. The table's gloss for Mizutani ('near Kalsi', Dehra Dun district, 30°32'N 77°53'E) does not fit this site, which lies by Jagadhri in Ambala district; worth checking. The possible monastery enclosure is not linked to Xuanzang. See 191.
Excavation in Rajasthan; Mathura Mitra coins and Vaisali discs compared.

author: D. Mandal under G. R. Sharma, Allahabad University
evidence: 1963-64: 6-m stone wall on the Yamuna side traced for 52 m (rubble, then ashlar); stone stairway to a landing (Sub-period VI); vaulted roof 7.62 m wide over the E gallery (Sub-period X, 1st-2nd c. AD); dry ditch outside the N boundary wall from the NBP phase
quote: resumed excavation in the palace-area at Kausambi. Excavation revealed that the palace was defended by a massive wall on the Yamuna side also
note: Continues 127 and 150; no reference to Udayana or Xuanzang. City = Kosam (05.05).
Mainahai, 2.4 km E of the eastern gateway of Kausambi: Mauryan-style capitals and sculptures; not linked to any of Xuanzang's sites.
Lalitpur and PGW site; Kausambi pottery compared.
Nanur and Goswamikhanda excavations.

author: S. R. Das, Department of Archaeology, University of Calcutta
evidence: 1963-64: six structural phases; a long wall on natural soil enclosing the settlement against floods; Phase III granary; Phase VI circular stupa basement; many seals and sealings, palaeographically 6th-10th c. (central date 7th-8th c.), C-14 for Phase III 1200 ± 80 BP; sealings naming the Raktamrittika-vihara and its acharya-bhikshu
quote: On palaeographical grounds, they are assignable to a period between the sixth and the tenth century A.D., with a central date around the seventh-eighth century … Some of the sealings refer to the illustrious Raktamrittika-vihara and its acharya-bhikshu.
note: More sealings naming the monastery, with Phase III dated to Xuanzang's time: confirms Mizutani's 10.08.02 and supports 10.08 (Rangamati); asr (Beglar: Dulmi) and ar (Dikshit's doubt) superseded for the monastery.
Epigraphy (Kausambi seals of Dhanabhuti and yaksha-Dhanasri); no location.
Persian and Arabic inscriptions.
Coins (Kausambi kings) and minor discoveries (neolithic celt at Rajgir).
Minor discoveries and museums (Sarnath votive stupa images; Allahabad seals).
Museums.
Conservation (Nalanda, Kumrahar, Ramabhar, Kusinagara, Sarnath).
Gardens.
Conservation and publications.
Plate captions.

author: K. Raghavachary, South-eastern Circle, ASI
asr_identification: habitation area within the fortifications of Dharanikota (Guntur)
evidence: 1964-65: habitation from the toe of the rampart; Period I megalithic Black-and-red Ware; II post-holes, drains, goldsmith's mould, glass bangles; III Rouletted Ware, soak-pits; IV circular brick structure, grey ware dominant
quote: resumed excavation at sites DKT-1 and DKT-3. The objective of this season's dig Was to locate the habitation-area within the fortifications
note: Continues 147 and 159; no reference to Dhanyakataka or Xuanzang. Mizutani's capital near Dharanikota (10.14).
Kaveripattinam and Uraiyur; Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda style compared.
Explorations in Karnal; PGW at Astipur and other villages near Thanesar listed; no identification (cf. Mizutani's Asthipur, 04.08.02).

author: N. R. Banerjee, ASI headquarters, with N. C. Ghosh, M. C. Joshi and H. K. Narain
evidence: 1964-65: Ochre-coloured Ware (Period I, c. 60 cm) below the PGW; sequence revised to OCW I, PGW II, NBP III, Kushan-Gupta IV; confirmed on a second, higher mound
quote: Excavation was resumed at the fortified site of Ahichchhatra (fig. 7) by the headquarters office of the Survey under Dr. N. R. Banerjee … the Northern Black Polished Ware and the associated cultural assemblage as Period III, and the last phase, with Kushan and Gupta relics, as Period IV.
note: Agrees with Mizutani's Ahicchattra at Ramnagar (04.13) and Cunningham's Adikot (asr); nothing on Xuanzang's period or his monasteries.

author: S. R. Das, Department of Archaeology, University of Calcutta
evidence: 1964-65: six phases; Phase III-IV panchayatana temple-complex (enclosure wall 20.87 m with four corner shrines, triratha main temple, mandapa); Phases IV-V oblong temple-complex; no new inscription reported
quote: Structures of Phase III to which belonged the pan-chayatana temple-complex were built on the ddbris of Phase II.
note: Continues 152 and 166. A Brahmanical temple complex beside the monastery from Phase III (6th-7th c.); the report does not relate it to Xuanzang's description of Karnasuvarna. Mizutani 10.08, 10.08.02.
Minor discoveries and museums.

Title page and contents.
Kesanapalli stupa (Guntur) discovered; Amaravati idiom compared.
Explorations near Ajanta.

author: B. Ch. Chhabra, assisted by Suraj Bhan, Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture, Punjab University
asr_identification: Sugh (Ambala): inscribed clay sealing with the legend Sugha (3rd c. AD)
evidence: 1965-66: Sub-period I A (c. 600-500 BC) late PGW with NBP; I B (c. 500-100 BC) brick houses, terracotta drain-pipes, punch-marked and Indo-Greek coins, coin legend hadasa; Period II (c. 100 BC-AD 500) metal-working, sealings with the legends Vyagharaja and Sugha in 3rd-c. AD characters
quote: Sub-period I B (circa 500-100 B.C.) was distinguished by the absence of the Painted Grey Ware … inscribed clay sealings, one bearing the legend Vyagharaja and the other Sugha, both in the third century A.D. characters.
note: Inscribed find naming the place: the 'Sugha' sealing confirms Sugh = Srughna (Cunningham, asr; Mizutani 04.09). The report does not name Srughna or Xuanzang, and its sequence ends c. AD 500, before his visit.
Exploration table (Saharanpur district).

author: Y. D. Sharma, Northern Circle, ASI
asr_identification: mound near Kashipur (Naini Tal), with the Bhima-gaja hump
evidence: 1965-66: S wall of a brick temple plinth 29.5 m long and 5.95 m high with seven chaitya-window motifs, dated on style to the 6th-8th c.; disused after the 12th-13th c.; pottery like Ahichchhatra Stratum III (AD 350-750); PGW the earliest ware; earlier finds: Krishna Deva's 1939-40 dig, a Trivikrama image, NBP sherds, Kushan gold coins
quote: conducted a limited excavation on the mound near Kashipur, identified by General Cunningham with Kiu-pi-shwang-na of the Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang, which is rendered by Julien as Govisana … The exposed walls, obviously belonging to the high plinth of a temple, may be assigned, on stylistic grounds, to a period between sixth to eighth centuries A.D.
note: Cites Cunningham's identification without arguing it. Agrees with Mizutani 04.12 (ruins 1 mile E of Kashipur) and asr (old fort of Ujain); a temple of Xuanzang's age is consistent with the deva temples he counts at Govisana; no inscription naming the place.
Epigraphy (Mathura Buddhist image inscriptions).
Coins and minor discoveries.
Radiocarbon dates (Dharanikota fortifications c. 205 BC); no identification.
